subject.title: [Feature]: Support configurable request labels for Gemini API calls (GCP billing tracking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public Google Vertex request-label config contract for billing attribution, and should it be limited to static Vertex-only labels with strict GCP validation?
rationale: This adds a new provider config surface and can expose operator metadata in billing systems, so code inspection can prove the gap but not choose the product/privacy boundary.

options.title: Approve bounded Vertex labels
options.body: Add a `google-vertex`-scoped static label map with documented GCP key/value validation and no dynamic session/agent labels until separately approved.

options.title: Defer dynamic attribution
options.body: Keep the issue open but require a deeper design for agent/skill/session-derived labels and privacy/cardinality limits before implementation.

options.title: Decline core config surface
options.body: Close as not planned if maintainers decide cost-attribution labels should be handled by an external proxy or deployment-specific integration instead of OpenClaw config.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Vertex labels
recommendation.body: Add a `google-vertex`-scoped static label map with documented GCP key/value validation and no dynamic session/agent labels until separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The Google transport and config-surface history points most strongly to this owner for deciding whether the new provider config belongs in the bundled Google plugin.
